paper_id: Pretraining without Wordpieces_ Learning Over a Vocabulary of Millions of Words
title: Pretraining without Wordpieces: Learning Over a Vocabulary of Millions of Words
motivation: subword tokenization breaks words into pieces, causing inconvenience in word-level representation and cloze prediction
problem_framing: exploring BERT-style pretraining over word-level vocabulary without subword decomposition
key_insight: word-level vocabulary avoids subword fragmentation issues; main advantage is better understanding of low-frequency and rare words
method_signature: WordBERT with multi-million word vocabulary, sampling-based softmax training, Transformer architecture
evaluation_criteria: cloze test accuracy, machine reading comprehension (EM/F1), POS/chunking/NER F1, probing accuracy across word frequencies
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: WordBERT-Glove underperforms randomly initialized versions; larger vocab causes slower softmax on probing task
evidence_for_taste: the major advantage lies in understanding for low-frequency words
BERT tends to generate general words
our models are able to learn better representation for medium-frequency words
it has comparable time cost to BERT
thinking_moves: 识别subword分词在词级任务上的工程不便
系统性探索不同词表大小(500K, 1M)和初始化策略(Glove)的差异
通过probing分析定位模型提升的具体来源(低频词理解)
跨语言验证语言无关性(中英双语实验)
承认OOV问题但论证其影响有限
